title: HIVE Doctor — which professional to see
author: Jeff
review_status: UNVERIFIED — requires clinician sign-off; referral pathways vary by country/health system
start_note: In most places you start with your GP / family doctor (or a walk-in / urgent care). They treat many of these themselves and refer you to the right specialist when it's needed.

by_system.mental: mental-health support — your GP, a counsellor or a psychiatrist
by_system.mh: mental-health support — your GP, a counsellor or a psychiatrist
by_system.msk: an orthopaedic or rheumatology specialist, and a physiotherapist
by_system.onc: your GP first, for an urgent specialist referral

overrides.anaphylaxis: emergency department now, then an allergy specialist
overrides.aortic_dissection: emergency department now (call your local emergency number)
overrides.pulmonary_embolism: emergency department now, then respiratory / haematology
overrides.stroke: emergency department now (call your local emergency number), then neurology/stroke team
overrides.meningitis: emergency department now (call your local emergency number)
overrides.sepsis: emergency department now (call your local emergency number)
overrides.dka: emergency department now, then your diabetes team
overrides.opioid_overdose: emergency department now (call your local emergency number)
overrides.co_poisoning: emergency department now (and get the source checked)
overrides.cauda_equina: emergency department now, then spinal surgery
overrides.gca: same-day: rheumatology with ophthalmology — steroids cannot wait
overrides.hypertension: your GP, who may involve a cardiologist
overrides.ectopic: an early-pregnancy unit / emergency care now
overrides.encephalitis: emergency department now (call your local emergency number)
overrides.epiglottitis: emergency department now — keep upright and calm
overrides.ckd: your GP, then a kidney specialist (nephrologist)
overrides.alcohol_poisoning: emergency department now (call your local emergency number)
overrides.dental_trauma: a dentist now (within an hour for a knocked-out tooth)
overrides.hyperglycemia: your diabetes team (emergency if DKA signs)
overrides.tuberculosis: a doctor or TB/public-health clinic soon — treatment is usually free and confidential
overrides.androgenetic_alopecia: a pharmacist or GP (a dermatologist for uncertain or rapid loss)
